evidence.finding: Current candidate grammar restricts NAME and REF to ASCII-compatible regexes while STRING uses the parser string literal facility.
Prior executable research established that canonicalization must be type-directed and separated semantic_hash, artifact_hash, contract_hash and deployment/execution identity.

12665 canonical-equivalence pairs and 2411 compatibility-only pairs passed the exact-vs-explicit-NFC typed policy; global normalization counterexamples and concat boundary counterexamples were reproduced.

evidence.source: Unicode Standard Annex #15, Unicode Normalization Forms, current published Version 17.0.0, 2025-07-30
evidence.finding: Defines canonical versus compatibility equivalence, NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD, warns that compatibility normalization is context-sensitive, and states normalization forms are not closed under concatenation.

evidence.source: Unicode Standard Annex #31, Unicode Identifiers and Syntax
evidence.finding: Identifier specifications should define normalization/profile behavior; NFC is the straightforward policy for canonical-equivalent identifier handling when Unicode identifiers are supported.
A deterministic canonical wire format can preserve Unicode string data as-is rather than performing Unicode normalization; invalid lone-surrogate data is rejected.

ancestry_notes: The local typed-policy result extends the earlier ClayCode type-directed canonicalization lineage and is not counted as independent replication of that general principle.
